Subject: RFP follow-up: observability archive bids & clarification on log export / cold storage

Team / vendors — quick follow-up from the RFP bundle we sent last week. BigBank is very interested in a 12–18 month pilot but needs clarity on long-term archive economics and operational details before they sign. Can each vendor answer the bullets below and attach a short quote / SOW draft?

Key questions for quotes (short answers ok):
- Retention tiers: cost per GB/month for 30d, 90d, 1y, 3y (ingest vs stored).
- Cold storage: is retrieval charged separately? per-GB and per-request examples.
- Native long-term export: supported destinations (S3/GCS/Azure), who pays egress, and what format (Parquet, Loki chunks, JSONL)?
- Search & rehydration time SLA for archived data (e.g., <24h / <6h).
- Any required tooling/handoff for compliance audits (SOC 2 logs, WORM).

Attachments: SOW_template_v2.docx (attached) — please use this as a skeleton for contract terms and include an anticipated lead time for provisioning a pilot environment.

Next steps: I want vendor answers before Friday EOD so we can put numbers into a preliminary TCO. Monique (BigBank) — please flag any must-haves we missed.

Thanks,
Grace

Hi Grace — thanks for the concise list. Quick answers below and I attached a quote PDF with line items for a 12-month pilot. Happy to jump on a call.

- Retention tiers (Datadog typical public list pricing, discounts applied for pilot): ingest fees vary by log type; stored: 30d = $0.10/GB/mo, 90d = $0.07/GB/mo, 1y = $0.045/GB/mo, 3y = $0.028/GB/mo (example blended).
- Cold storage & retrieval: retrieval is charged — typical cold retrieval $0.02–$0.05/GB plus request fees; can provide a predictable monthly cap for pilots.
- Native export: S3 and GCS supported; export format is gzipped JSONL by default, Parquet available via managed export job. Egress responsibility is negotiated — for standard pilots Datadog covers export egress up to a small threshold; beyond that BigBank covers cloud egress.
- Rehydration SLA: best-effort rehydration <24h for bulk reingest; we can offer 6–12h SLA as a paid add-on.
- Compliance: we can provide archived index manifests and signed hashes for WORM setups; SOC 2 evidence kits are provided as part of enterprise onboarding.

See attachment: Datadog_quote_Q1_2026.pdf — contains line items (pilot cluster, retention add-on, export runbook).

Regards,

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: observability archive bids & clarification on log export / cold storage

Hi Grace — appreciate the list. Short answers and a proposal attached.

- Retention tiers (Grafana Cloud Indexed Logs): 30d = $0.085/GB/mo, 90d = $0.06/GB/mo, 1y = $0.035/GB/mo. Loki long-term storage (object storage) billed separately: storage in customer bucket at cloud provider rates + Grafana management fee ($0.005–$0.02/GB/mo depending on commitment).
- Cold retrieval: retrieval depends on the bucket provider; Grafana does not add retrieval per-GB charges beyond the management fee but retrieval latency depends on your bucket class.
- Native export: supports S3/GCS/Azure Blob; Loki uses chunk encoding — export is to customer bucket; typically customer pays egress to the bucket. Parquet export is not native but we provide a conversion pipeline as a deliverable for pilots.
- Rehydration SLA: Loki reindexing of archived chunks is usually <12h for focused queries; bulk restores depend on bucket performance.
- Compliance: we provide manifest files and a compliance integration guide; we can sign off on audit artifacts.

Proposal attached: GrafanaCloud_proposal.xlsx — includes a 3-month free ingest window for pilot customers and an optional managed long-term storage onboarding.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Strategic Accounts — Grafana Cloud

Grace / team — quick internal take after reading the two vendor replies:
- Datadog gives clearer SLA options for rehydration and seems willing to cap export egress for pilots (nice).
- Grafana's Loki approach offloads storage to customer buckets which probably lowers ongoing storage costs but shifts egress/restore ops to the customer.
- We should model both: a Datadog-managed retention (higher predictable $/GB but easier for compliance) and a Grafana-bucket approach (lower storage $ but potential unexpected egress).

Question: do we want Sentry or a specialized log archival vendor in scope? Sentry handles error events but not long-term indexable logs. If BigBank wants full-fidelity for compliance they may prefer vendor-managed retention.

I'm in favor of a 3-month technical pilot + 9–12 month commercial pilot. I'll draft a quick cost sketch and share.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

Adding my cost sketch (attached) and recommendation:

Summary: for BigBank's estimated 60 TB/month ingest of logs (post-filtering), a blended 12-month pilot with Grafana long-term storage + Datadog for metrics/alerts reduces vendor lock and keeps compliance artifacts accessible. I modeled three scenarios (attached obs_cost_sketch.csv):
- Vendor-managed retention (Datadog primary): higher monthly line item, predictable egress allowances, recommended if BigBank wants minimal ops overhead.
- Customer-bucket retention (Grafana Loki): lowest recurring storage, but include a monthly egress reserve and runbook for rehydration testing.
- Hybrid: Datadog for indexed logs (30–90d) + Grafana for 1y+ archive. This is my preferred path.

I also noted contract items to negotiate: SLA on archive retrieval windows, a capped egress allowance for pilot, and an audit runbook for SOC 2 reviewers.

Attachment: obs_cost_sketch.csv (CSV, 6 KB). I'll be ready to present numbers on Tue 11 Feb.

Marissa
